questions.question: A sum of Rs 12,500 is invested at 8% p.a. simple interest for 3 years. Find the interest earned.
questions.trick: SI = PRT/100. Just multiply P by R by T and drop two zeros.

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs 15,000 at 10% p.a. compounded annually for 2 years.
The difference between the compound interest and simple interest on a certain sum for 2 years at 12% p.a. is Rs 288. Find the sum.
At what rate percent per annum will a sum of money double itself in 8 years at simple interest?
questions.solution: To double at SI, interest = principal, so PRT/100 = P → R x 8 = 100 → R = 100/8 = **12.5%**.
questions.trick: Rate to multiply to n times in T years at SI = (n−1) x 100 / T = (2−1) x 100 / 8 = 12.5%.

questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs 9,680 in 2 years at 10% p.a. compound interest. Find the principal.
questions.trick: P = Amount / (1 + R/100)^T. Divide 9680 by 1.21.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 800 and sells it for Rs 920. Find the profit percent.
questions.trick: Profit% = (SP − CP)/CP x 100.

questions.question: By selling an article for Rs 1,140, a man loses 5%. Find the cost price.
A trader marks his goods 40% above cost price and then allows a discount of 25%. Find his profit or loss percent.
A man sells two articles at Rs 990 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. Find his overall profit or loss percent.
questions.solution:
Selling two items at equal price with equal +x% and −x% always gives a loss of x²/100 = 10²/100 = **1% loss**.
(Check: CP₁ = 990/1.1 = 900, CP₂ = 990/0.9 = 1100; total CP = 2000, total SP = 1980 → 20 loss on 2000 = 1%.)
questions.trick: Same SP, gain x% and loss x% → always x²/100 loss.

questions.question: The cost price of 15 articles equals the selling price of 12 articles. Find the profit percent.
questions.trick: If CP of A articles = SP of B articles, Profit% = (A − B)/B x 100.

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
A and B together can do a work in 10 days, while A alone can do it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone complete it?
A is twice as efficient as B, and together they finish a work in 14 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.solution: A:B efficiency = 2:1, combined 3 units/day. Total work = 3 x 14 = 42 units. A alone = 42/2 = **21 days**.
questions.trick: More efficient one alone = together time x (sum of ratio)/(its own ratio) = 14 x 3/2 = 21.

questions.question: 15 men can complete a work in 20 days. How many days will 25 men take to do the same work?
questions.trick: M₁D₁ = M₂D₂ → D₂ = (15 x 20)/25 = 12.

questions.question: A can do a work in 24 days. He works for 6 days and then leaves. B finishes the remaining work in 12 days. In how many days can B alone complete the whole work?
questions.solution: A does 6/24 = 1/4 in 6 days. Remaining 3/4 done by B in 12 days → B's full-work time = 12 ÷ (3/4) = **16 days**.
questions.trick: If a fraction f is done in t days, whole job = t/f = 12/(3/4) = 16.

questions.question: A train 180 m long crosses a pole in 12 seconds. Find its speed in km/h.
questions.trick: m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a platform 250 m long in 20 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.trick: Train length = (speed in m/s x time) − platform length.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m run in opposite directions at 40 km/h and 50 km/h. In how much time will they cross each other?
questions.solution: Opposite direction → relative speed = 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. Total length = 300 m. Time = 300/25 = **12 s**.
questions.trick: Crossing time = (L₁ + L₂)/relative speed; add speeds when opposite.

questions.question: A boat goes 30 km downstream in 2 hours and 30 km upstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water.
questions.solution: Downstream = 30/2 = 15 km/h; upstream = 30/3 = 10 km/h. Still water = (15 + 10)/2 = **12.5 km/h**.
questions.trick: Boat speed = (down + up)/2.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the stream is 3 km/h. Find the total time to go 36 km downstream and return to the starting point.
questions.trick: Downstream = b + s, upstream = b − s; add the two times.

questions.question: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 24. Find the largest of these numbers.
questions.solution: For 5 consecutive even numbers the middle one is the average = 24, so numbers are 20, 22, 24, 26, 28 → largest = **28**.
questions.trick: For an odd count of equally-spaced numbers, average = middle term; largest = average + 2 x (gap x steps) = 24 + 4 = 28.

questions.question: The average age of 30 students in a class is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average rises to 15 years. Find the teacher's age.
questions.solution: Students' total = 30 x 14 = 420. New total = 31 x 15 = 465. Teacher = 465 − 420 = **45**.
questions.trick: New member's value = new avg + (old count) x (rise) = 15 + 30 x 1 = 45.

questions.question: The average of 10 numbers is 45. If each number is increased by 8, what will be the new average?
questions.solution: Adding the same 8 to every number raises the average by 8: 45 + 8 = **53**.
questions.trick: Add k to each item → average increases by k.

questions.question: A batsman has an average of 36 runs in 16 innings. In his 17th innings he scores 70 runs. Find his new average.
questions.solution: Total after 17 innings = 16 x 36 + 70 = 576 + 70 = 646. New average = 646/17 = **38**.
questions.trick: New avg = (old total + new score)/new count.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5:7. After 6 years the ratio becomes 3:4. Find the present age of A.
questions.trick: Cross-multiply the future ratio and solve for x.

questions.question: A father is 4 times as old as his son. After 10 years he will be twice as old as his son. Find the present age of the son.
questions.solution:
Let son = s, father = 4s. 4s + 10 = 2(s + 10) → 4s + 10 = 2s + 20 → 2s = 10 → s = **5**.
(Check: 20 & 5 now; 30 & 15 later → twice.)
questions.trick: Frame one equation from the "after 10 years" condition.

questions.question: The sum of the present ages of a mother and her daughter is 50 years. Five years ago the mother was 4 times as old as her daughter. Find the daughter's present age.
questions.trick: Substitute the sum relation into the past-age relation.

questions.question: The present age of A is 3 times that of B. Five years hence, the sum of their ages will be 50 years. Find the present age of A.
questions.trick: Write both future ages, add, and solve.

questions.question: Rs 3,600 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 2:3:4. Find C's share.
questions.trick: Share = (own ratio/total ratio) x amount.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3:5. If 8 is added to each, the ratio becomes 2:3. Find the two numbers.
questions.trick: Cross-multiply after adding the constant to each term.

questions.question: If A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5, find A:B:C.
questions.trick: Scale each ratio so the shared term (B) matches.

questions.question: The ratio of boys to girls in a class is 7:5. If there are 12 more boys than girls, find the total number of students.
questions.trick: Difference in parts equals given difference → find x, multiply by total parts.

questions.question: If 35% of a number is 140, find the number.
questions.trick: If p% of N = value, then N = value x 100/p.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the winner secured 60% of the total votes and won by 800 votes. Find the total number of votes polled.
questions.solution: Winner 60%, loser 40%, margin = 20% = 800 votes → total = 800 x 100/20 = **4,000**.
questions.trick: Margin% = winner% − loser%; total = margin votes x 100/margin%.

questions.question: The price of an article is increased by 20%. By what percent must it now be reduced to bring it back to the original price?
questions.solution: Required reduction = increase/(100 + increase) x 100 = 20/120 x 100 = **16⅔%**.
questions.trick: To undo an x% rise, reduce by [x/(100 + x)] x 100.

questions.question: A student scored 30% marks and failed by 40 marks. The passing mark is 40%. Find the maximum marks of the examination.
questions.solution: Pass mark = 40%, student got 30% and fell short by 40 marks → 10% of max = 40 → max = **400**.
questions.trick: (pass% − scored%) of max = shortfall; max = shortfall x 100/(difference%).

questions.question: A person's salary is first increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. Find the net percentage change in the salary.
questions.trick: Successive +a% and −b%: net = a − b − (ab/100) = 10 − 10 − 1 = −1%.

questions.question: In what ratio must rice costing Rs 30/kg be mixed with rice costing Rs 45/kg so that the mixture is worth Rs 40/kg?
questions.trick: Ratio = (dearer − mean):(mean − cheaper).

questions.question: A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7:3. How much water must be added to make the ratio 3:2?
questions.solution: In 60 L: milk = 42, water = 18. Milk unchanged; for 3:2 water must be 42 x 2/3 = 28. Add 28 − 18 = **10 litres**.
questions.trick: Keep the unchanged quantity fixed, compute the new required amount of the other.

questions.question: A vessel contains 40 litres of pure milk. 8 litres is drawn out and replaced with water; this is done a second time. Find the quantity of milk left in the vessel.
questions.trick: After n replacements: remaining = Initial x (1 − drawn/total)^n.

questions.question: In what ratio must water be mixed with milk costing Rs 24 per litre so that by selling the mixture at Rs 24 per litre one gains 25%?
questions.solution: To gain 25% selling at Rs 24, cost of mixture = 24/1.25 = Rs 19.2/L. Alligation of water (0) and milk (24) about 19.2: water:milk = (24 − 19.2):(19.2 − 0) = 4.8:19.2 = **1:4**.
questions.trick: Cost of mix = SP/(1 + gain%); then alligate water (cost 0) with milk.

questions.question: A and B invest Rs 25,000 and Rs 35,000 respectively in a business. If the total profit is Rs 12,000, find B's share.
questions.trick: Equal time → profit split in capital ratio.

questions.question: A starts a business with Rs 20,000. After 4 months B joins with Rs 30,000. Find the ratio in which the year-end profit should be divided.
questions.trick: Profit ratio = (capital x time) for each partner.

questions.question: A, B and C invest in a business in the ratio 3:4:5 for the same period. If C's share of the profit is Rs 2,500, find the total profit.
questions.trick: Total = (one share) x (total parts/that partner's parts).

questions.question: A invests Rs 10,000 for 8 months and B invests Rs 12,000 for 5 months in a business. Find the ratio in which they should share the profit.
questions.trick: Profit ratio = capital x time; then reduce.

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 20 minutes and pipe B in 30 minutes. If both are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.trick: Together time = (ab)/(a + b) = (20 x 30)/50 = 12.

questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 15 hours. A leak at the bottom can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If both operate together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.trick: Fill minus leak: net = 1/fill − 1/leak; time = reciprocal.

questions.question: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 24 and 32 minutes respectively. Both are opened together. After how many minutes should B be closed so that the tank is full in 18 minutes?
questions.solution: A runs the full 18 min → 18/24 = 3/4 filled. B must fill remaining 1/4 → B's time t/32 = 1/4 → t = **8 minutes**.
questions.trick: Fraction by the always-open pipe first, then find how long the other pipe supplies the rest.

questions.question: A cistern is normally filled by a tap in 8 hours, but due to a leak it takes 2 hours longer. If the cistern is full, how long will the leak alone take to empty it?
questions.solution: With leak it takes 8 + 2 = 10 h. Leak rate = 1/8 − 1/10 = 5/40 − 4/40 = 1/40 → **40 hours**.
questions.trick: Leak rate = 1/(fill time) − 1/(actual time); invert for emptying time.

questions.question: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in 10, 15 and 30 minutes respectively. If all three are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
questions.trick: Add the individual rates (use LCM as the work unit) and take the reciprocal.
